extracted.intended_audience: government agencies and public servants conducting public consultations; interested members of the public and parliamentarians
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and government practice for designing and running public consultations (choice of platform, duration, engagement mode, training/tools, and objectives) used by Singapore government agencies. Focuses on fit-for-purpose design rather than a single prescriptive rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation duration categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultations are classified by duration into: (i) two weeks or shorter; (ii) more than two weeks and less than one month; and (iii) more than one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 2016–2020 REACH hosted 113 consultations: 58 lasted between 2 weeks and 1 month, and 53 lasted more than 1 month. These counts are illustrative of past practice for consultations published on REACH but represent only a slice of overall engagement efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of REACH website to solicit public views
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government uses the REACH website to seek views from members of the public across a range of issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: REACH is a principal online platform for public consultations but is not the only engagement channel; agencies may use REACH where appropriate for public-facing consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit-for-purpose engagement mode
rubrics_metrics.description: The engagement mode must be fit-for-purpose: the design, duration, and target audience will vary according to the policy issue at hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose among dialogues, people-private-public (3P) committees, focus group discussions, online consultations or other modes depending on objectives and stakeholders. Examples cited include SGFuture, Committee on the Future Economy, and the Land Transport Master Plan 2040.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor design, duration and target audience to the policy issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Design elements (including duration) and the intended audience should be tailored to the particular policy question being addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no one-size-fits-all timetable or format; agencies should select parameters that best meet the consultation's objectives and the needs of intended participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide training and resources to level up engagement capability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Service offers a suite of training programmes and resources that distill the principles and best practices of public engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are expected to use and continually update these training programmes and resources, and to learn from experience and external experts to improve engagement quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use field guides and digital tools to carry out engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: There are field guides and digital tools to help agencies carry out engagements that best meet their objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field guides and digital tools are intended to support practical delivery of consultations and should be used to design processes that achieve stated objectives and accessibility for stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure a meaningful experience for stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagements should ensure a meaningful experience for stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningful experience is an explicit objective tied to the use of training, field guides, tools and appropriate engagement modes — not merely soliciting responses but enabling substantive participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move beyond consultation to partnering, co-creation and co-delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government seeks to go beyond one-way consultation toward partnering with citizens to co-create and co-deliver solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies and initiatives may involve citizens in design and implementation (examples: Singapore Together, Recycle Right Citizens' Workgroup 2019, SG Youth Action Plan 2019), and the COVID-19 response showed citizen groups partnering with government in practical ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple engagement avenues beyond REACH
rubrics_metrics.description: Government engagement includes many channels beyond online consultations on REACH, such as dialogues, 3P committees, and focus groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider a mix of channels (national dialogues, targeted committees, focus groups, citizen workgroups, etc.) appropriate to the topic and stakeholders to broaden participation and depth of feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fixed universal minimum consultation duration (policy position)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government did not adopt a blanket rule that all public consultations must run for at least one month; duration is determined by fit-for-purpose considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While a parliamentarian asked whether consultations should run no shorter than one month, the response emphasises tailoring duration to objectives and issue complexity rather than imposing a uniform minimum; agencies use judgement supported by training and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and report consultation statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government collects and reports basic statistics on consultations (e.g., counts and durations for consultations hosted on REACH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published figures (113 consultations from 2016–2020 on REACH, with breakdowns by duration) illustrate that agencies track consultation activity and durations, though REACH figures represent only part of total engagement activity.
